objective: Add a bounded append-only interaction-segment commitment ledger binding ordered span commitments to capability freshness, delegation chain, route, task/artifact context, policy generation, expiry, and terminal verification without storing raw content or claiming behavioral reproducibility.

research_inputs.finding: Agent governance separates capability integrity, behavioral verifiability, and interaction auditability; verifiable interaction ledgers can bind identity/capability evidence to hash-linked records, while reproducibility assumptions remain model-dependent.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL implements only commitment and continuity checks and explicitly records that models were not replayed and behavior was not independently reproduced.

research_inputs.finding: A2A tasks and artifacts provide durable task/context lineage and artifacts persist through task completion or explicit deletion.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The ledger binds trace segments to task and artifact identifiers and terminal evidence without creating tasks, mutating artifacts, or replacing A2A transport semantics.

research_inputs.finding: OpenTelemetry provides interoperable traces, metrics, and logs, but telemetry is an observation and not kernel-level ground truth.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract accepts caller-supplied span commitments without ingesting OTLP, storing raw prompts/outputs, or promoting telemetry into truth or authority.

features: trace sequence starts at one and remains contiguous
bounded segment/request expiry and trace span count
mandatory terminal verification for the active policy
raw-content minimization and explicit non-authority boundary

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane commitment overhead; excludes signatures, OTLP ingestion, model replay, network, tools, storage, accelerator, and kernel scheduling latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the interaction-ledger module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged capability-freshness release

limitations: The ledger validates caller-supplied span commitments and does not verify that a span corresponds to a real process, model, tool, or network event.
No cryptographic signatures, independent verifier, remote anchor, OTLP ingestion, model replay, or behavioral reproducibility test was performed.
The benchmark measures local Python commitment overhead and excludes cryptography, network, storage, model, tool, accelerator, and kernel scheduler performance.
The real-task validation is a deterministic local fixture and does not establish multi-host interoperability, agent quality, general intelligence, browser autonomy, robotics, or production efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
